The finding

The question. Gemma-3-12B-IT refuses more in Slovene than in English. Is it better at spotting harm in Slovene, or does it just refuse more readily? Its Slovene-adapted sibling, GaMS3-12B-Instruct, starts from the same base model and serves as the comparison.

The answer. Unedited Gemma benign Slovene items at , against in English. Its hit rate on harmful items rises only from 0.89 to 0.94. puts the whole gap in the , not in . GaMS3 shows no such shift.

= , the criterion shift of Gemma toward refusal in Slovene relative to GaMS3 (Experiment 5, 1,093 safe and 349 harmful items). The same contrast on d′ is .

The paper reports this as replicated across four experiments. Change the item set, the coding or the English arm in the chart panel to see which of those choices the result depends on.

      Try it: move the judge's decision threshold

      The Qwen3-14B judge records a probability for each of its three labels, and the paper takes the most probable one. Here you can call an answer a refusal whenever its probability passes a threshold of your choice, and the page recomputes every rate and both contrasts over the 1,093 safe and 349 harmful items in each of the four model × language cells.

      What the paper says it does not show

      • The reply-language result is an estimate. For Gemma at high dose, the raw output-language contrast is OUTSL = log-odds. The -corrected value is , consistent with zero, and the pre-registered four-readout robustness gate returns robust = .
      • The judge anchor is weak in the decisive cell. The adjudicator agrees with the primary judge at κ = 0.12 in the Gemma Slovene-edited cell (Se = 0.927, Sp = 0.714, n = 48), so roughly 29% of non-refusals there are scored as refusals. The adjudicator is itself an LLM (Sonnet 4.5), not a human.
      • Four grid cells fail . SL→EN, HU→EN, SL→HU and HU→SL fall under 90% for GaMS3, so off the English-input row those cells do not measure the requested reply language. Restricted to compliant English-input rows, the edit-induced lag in EN→SL is .
      • The unedited cross-model gap is inconclusive. In the SL→SL cell, unedited GaMS3 sits −1.17 [−2.83, 0.22] below Gemma. The fragility index is 1, and both models are near ceiling (Gemma 0.95, GaMS3 0.87).
      • Hungarian and RefusEU are uninformative. The minimum detectable effect for Hungarian is about 3 log-odds units. The RefusEU DiD (Experiment 17) is inconclusive (MDE > 2) because refusal there is near ceiling.
      • Other limits. Both models run in NF4, and the edit's interaction with quantization is not characterised. Slovene items are machine-translated and not checked by a native speaker. The adjudication sample is 30 items per cell. Language-dependent over-refusal is partly anticipated by prior work; the paper's contribution is the criterion-versus-sensitivity decomposition and the controlled edit design.
